title: Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman places him among the leading sages of the generation in Rava’s time, and both received from Rav Nachman, as in Beitzah 34b, where Rava asked Rav Nachman and Mar Zutra said of this, “We too have learned it.”

In Sotah 10a he asked Rav Nachman, “What is podagra like?” In Gittin 50a he spoke in Rav Nachman’s name, and Abaye said, “Know.” In Bava Batra 151b: “The Rabbis said it before Rava in the name of Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman, who said it in Rav Nachman’s name”; and so it is in Avodah Zarah 37b. In Bava Batra 7a Hyman considers “before Rabbah” erroneous and proposes “Rava.”

In Chullin 94b he was going from Sikhra to Bei Mechoza, and Rava and Rav Safra were coming to Sikhra; they met each other. He (Mar Zutra) thought they were coming to meet him, and said to them: “Why did the Rabbis trouble so much?” Rav Safra said to him: “We did not know that the Master was coming; had we known, we would have troubled more.” His halakhot we find in Berakhot 43b, Shabbat 88b and 96a, Bava Metzia 4b and 88b; and his well-known ruling in Gittin 49b, that he holds a woman’s ketubah is from middle-grade land, on which Abaye and Rava said, “Come and hear.” In Horayot 13a he said “Come and hear” on Rami bar Chama’s question, and some say he himself resolved it, saying, “Was it not stated on this: Rava said that Rav Nachman said” (see Rashi there). In Berakhot 54b he spoke to Rav Huna (Hon) son of Rav Nachman and resolved Rava’s words. Sanhedrin 5a relates that he judged a case and erred; he came before Rav Yosef, who said to him: “If they accepted you over them, you need not pay.” Learn from this that when one does not take authorization, his judgment is a valid judgment. Of his personal deeds we find that he was wealthy and scrupulous in his deeds, as in Moed Katan 12a: they built him a mansion by contract outside the boundary (on Shabbat); Rav Safra and Rav Huna bar Chinena visited and did not go in to him; some say he too did not go into it.

notes.text: The positive conclusion is retained: supplied דיניה דינא and saved Davidson Sanhedrin5a paragraph2 both conclude a judgment without authorization IS valid. The draft’s not a judgment is withdrawn. Restore the supplied Hon parenthetical. ר״ג in Gittin is expanded to Nachman contextually, disclosed; the case remains abridged. Hyman’s Rabbah-to-Rava proposal remains attributed.

The consulted Sanhedrin 5a explicitly concludes that judgment without authorization is valid, while distinguishing liability when the parties did not accept the judge. The withdrawn negative conclusion is not restored. Hon, the Nachman siglum and Hyman’s Rabbah/Rava proposal remain disclosed. His leading-generation and personal-life conclusions are not independently established by this one case.
